cards.title: Match search intent before writing anything
cards.summary: Sort target keywords by informational vs commercial intent so blog posts and service pages get pointed at the right query type.
cards.use_when: Product selection and content planning: deciding which keywords get a blog post, which get a landing/service page, and which to skip entirely.

cards.title: Filter keywords by difficulty and volume
cards.summary: Use an outside SEO tool to filter a root keyword down to terms with low difficulty and real search volume before committing content budget.
cards.use_when: Keyword research for blog posts, category pages or service pages where you need a shortlist worth producing.

cards.title: Build adjacent top-of-funnel topics to capture future buyers
cards.summary: Add keywords for the wider audience that will need your product later, not just the people ready to buy now.
cards.use_when: Content planning and acquisition: filling out the top of the funnel so prospects who are not yet shopping return to you when they are.

cards.title: Build keyword clusters so one page ranks for many queries
cards.summary: Give each page one root keyword plus a cluster of related terms so a single page can surface for dozens of queries.
cards.use_when: Producing a blog post, category page or landing page where you want maximum search coverage from one piece of content.

cards.title: Reverse-engineer the top-ranking pages into a template
cards.summary: Analyze the top non-forum results for a keyword, average their structure, and use that as the target format for your page.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting a page where you want to match what already ranks before adding your own differentiation.

cards.title: Train the AI on your voice, stories and stats before drafting
cards.summary: Feed the model reference files of your writing, humor, opinions and real business numbers so generated copy does not read as generic filler.
cards.use_when: Publishing any AI-drafted store content — product descriptions, buying guides, category or landing pages — where generic copy would hurt dwell time and trust.

cards.title: Batch a site build: pages, design reference and SOP file
cards.summary: Scaffold a structured site (homepage, blog index, service index) from a single prompt plus a design screenshot and an instruction file.
cards.use_when: Launching or restructuring a store's content architecture when you need index pages and templated landing pages fast without a developer.

cards.title: Check initial and rendered HTML on ecommerce money pages
cards.summary: Use server-rendered or static product content where practical, and verify crawler rendering before choosing an architecture.
cards.use_when: Technical SEO setup at site build time, when deciding how pages are rendered and whether crawlers can index them at all.

cards.title: Run a Lighthouse audit and hand the report to the agent to fix
cards.summary: Loop: run Lighthouse in the browser, expand the failing audits, paste the report into the coding agent, and iterate until scores hit 100.
cards.use_when: Technical SEO remediation on a new store or landing page before launch, and whenever page speed or crawlability issues are suspected.

cards.title: Generate sitemap and robots.txt so pages can be discovered
cards.summary: Emit a sitemap listing every page and a robots file granting crawler access, because unlisted pages cannot rank regardless of content quality.
cards.use_when: Technical SEO setup or post-launch, especially after adding many blog posts or landing pages.

cards.title: Apply an on-page checklist without destroying the content's voice
cards.summary: Run a standardized on-page optimization pass over every page, with an explicit instruction to keep the existing tone and humor intact.
cards.use_when: Optimizing blog posts, category pages or landing pages after drafting, before publishing.

cards.title: Separate content pages from money pages and let them feed each other
cards.summary: Blog content builds topical authority that lifts the commercial pages which actually generate leads and revenue.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much to invest in content versus commercial pages, and how to structure internal linking between them.

cards.title: Zip services and locations into landing pages — without overbuilding
cards.summary: Create one landing page per service-location (or service-category) pair for money keywords, kept visually consistent and deliberately limited in number.
cards.use_when: Landing page planning for a local or multi-market store that needs pages targeting '<service> <city>' style commercial queries.

cards.title: Reuse your best-converting landing page across all money pages
cards.summary: Test landing page variants to find the highest-converting structure, then apply that winning template to every commercial page.
cards.use_when: Landing page and PDP optimization: choosing what layout and copy structure to standardize across commercial pages.

cards.title: Package the whole workflow as a reusable skill
cards.summary: Encode the end-to-end content process as a repeatable command so one keyword trigger produces a fully optimized page.
cards.use_when: Scaling content production after you have proven the manual workflow on at least one page.

cards.title: Stage ecommerce content releases around review capacity
cards.summary: Release useful, verified content in manageable batches and monitor indexing.
cards.use_when: Replenishment and publishing cadence decisions when scaling content or launching many pages at once.

cards.title: Treat off-page SEO as optional and risky
cards.summary: The source stopped doing link-focused off-page SEO because algorithm updates repeatedly punished the sites that relied on it.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in backlink and off-site authority work versus on-site content and technical work.

cards.title: Rank for search to rank in AI answers
cards.summary: The source's position is that AI search visibility follows from ordinary search visibility, because AI tools retrieve answers from search engines.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to fund a separate 'AI SEO' or LLM-visibility workstream versus strengthening core search rankings.

cards.title: Optimize for content quality as the leading ranking lever
cards.summary: The source's mental model: Google profits from ads, ads need sustained attention, so Google rewards content that keeps people coming back.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing where to spend effort on a store's search program when you cannot address everything at once.

cards.title: Compress the whole SEO workflow into four buckets
cards.summary: Find winning keywords, then handle on-page, technical and off-page work as separate tracks, using automation to match teams you otherwise could not outstaff.
cards.use_when: Planning the scope of an SEO or organic acquisition program for a store and sequencing the work.

cards.title: Stage programmatic page publishing to avoid indexing penalties
cards.summary: Ramp new programmatic or blog pages gradually over roughly a week rather than bulk-publishing, because a sudden flood of pages risks Google penalties.
cards.use_when: Planning the rollout schedule for a large batch of programmatic landing pages, category pages or blog content on a store site.

cards.title: Why off-page link building is risky and often backfires
cards.summary: The presenter largely avoids off-page SEO because algorithm updates disproportionately punish sites that rely on backlink schemes, and even 'top 1%' backlinkers often produce declining results.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to budget for a backlink/off-page SEO agency or freelancer for your store.

cards.title: Broken backlink swapping as a legitimate link tactic
cards.summary: Find broken outbound links on competitor or industry sites using an SEO tool and offer to replace the dead link with your own relevant page.
cards.use_when: Building legitimate backlinks to a store's product or content pages without paying for spammy link schemes.

cards.title: Guest posting for backlinks via 'write for us' searches
cards.summary: Find sites that accept contributed articles by searching specific '[niche] + write for us' phrases and earn a backlink by authoring a post.
cards.use_when: Acquiring referral links and authority to a store or brand site through content contribution.

cards.title: Hero journalism (journalist query response) for expert backlinks
cards.summary: Answer journalists' open queries as an expert to earn a backlink when your answer is used.
cards.use_when: Building authority and backlinks for a niche store or brand with genuine subject-matter expertise.

cards.title: Paid quality backlinks from reputable domains
cards.summary: Pay reputable sites (the source cites Forbes and TechCrunch as possibly pay-to-play) to include a link to your site, leveraging their domain authority.
cards.use_when: Considering a paid placement to boost a store's domain authority and rankings — a fallback the source does not consider necessary.

cards.title: Deploy a Next.js site free with GitHub and Vercel
cards.summary: Push local site code to a private GitHub repo and connect it to Vercel to deploy live in about a minute, then add a custom domain.
cards.use_when: Taking a locally-hosted store or landing-page project live so the world can access it, using free hosting.

cards.title: Set up Google Search Console, verify ownership via HTML tag, and submit your sitemap
cards.summary: Connect a live store site to Google Search Console by adding a verification meta tag and submitting sitemap.xml so every page gets tracked.
cards.use_when: After deploying a store site, to start tracking search performance and get pages indexed.

cards.title: Request indexing of a new page in about a day
cards.summary: Use Search Console's URL inspection 'request indexing' to get a freshly deployed page into Google in about a day instead of weeks or months — with a daily request limit.
cards.use_when: After publishing a new landing page, product page or blog post, when you want it indexed quickly.

cards.title: Claim a free Google My Business listing as the lowest-hanging local win
cards.summary: A free Google My Business profile is described as the easiest way for local businesses to capture clicks, showing up prominently for local searches.
cards.use_when: Setting up local search presence for a store or service business that serves a geographic area.

cards.title: Post-launch SEO checklist order for a new store site
cards.summary: The source's post-deployment checklist: Google My Business, Search Console with sitemap, Google Analytics, then landing-page conversion testing.
cards.use_when: Running a systematic launch sequence after a store site or landing-page set goes live.

cards.title: Test landing pages to find the winning conversion formula, then roll it out
cards.summary: After launch, test your landing pages to identify the highest-converting version, then apply that formula to all existing pages.
cards.use_when: Optimizing an ecommerce site's landing pages after the site is live and has traffic to test with.

cards.title: Reuse a publishing skill across page types (blog and service pages)
cards.summary: The build-a-skill workflow used for blog content can be duplicated for service pages, extending the same production system across page types.
cards.use_when: Systematizing content production for a store — applying the same generation/rollout process to service or category pages after validating it on blog posts.

cards.title: Bottom-of-Funnel Keyword Targeting for Content ROI
cards.summary: Prioritize long-tail, high-intent keywords over broad top-of-funnel terms to maximize conversion potential from SEO content.
cards.use_when: Planning your SEO content calendar or deciding which keywords to target for blog posts meant to drive product sales.

cards.title: Internal Linking Loop Between Articles and Money Pages
cards.summary: Connect high-ranking informational content to money pages and back again to keep buyers engaged and build trust.
cards.use_when: Structuring site architecture and internal links between blog content and product or service pages.

cards.title: Set Up a Local Project Folder for AI Content Workflows
cards.summary: Run Claude Code from a local folder in an editor so all brand assets and generated content are saved and reusable on your machine.
cards.use_when: Setting up an AI-assisted SEO and content workflow and wanting your assets resident locally rather than external.

cards.title: Build Reusable Skills to Standardize Content Planning
cards.summary: Create persistent 'skills' once so you can later trigger repeatable content work with a single instruction instead of re-briefing each time.
cards.use_when: Repeatedly producing weekly blog and social content and wanting a repeatable, low-effort planning process.

cards.title: Automate Competitive Gap Analysis for Keyword Opportunities
cards.summary: Have the AI analyze local competitors to surface market gaps and duplicable opportunities before generating content titles.
cards.use_when: Starting keyword and topic research and looking for untapped angles competitors are missing or already winning.

cards.title: Use a Dedicated SEO Writer Tool for On-Page Optimization
cards.summary: Hand off approved titles/keywords to a specialized SEO content tool so built-in headings, metadata, and alt text are handled automatically.
cards.use_when: Producing SEO-optimized blog drafts at scale and wanting on-page elements handled without manual editing.

cards.title: Connect Content Tools via API for a Hands-Off Pipeline
cards.summary: Wire your AI agent to a content-generation API and your CMS so approved concepts flow straight to drafts without manual transfer.
cards.use_when: Building an automated SEO content pipeline and wanting to eliminate copy-paste between tools.

cards.title: Repurpose SEO Blog Content into Social Posts via RSS
cards.summary: Turn high-intent blog content into social posts so the same research drives social traffic back to articles and money pages.
cards.use_when: Extending an SEO content investment into social media and wanting social content aligned with proven high-intent topics.

cards.title: Integrate a Social Scheduling Tool for Automated Publishing
cards.summary: Connect a social scheduling platform via API so approved posts are queued and published on channel-specific time slots automatically.
cards.use_when: Automating social distribution of repurposed SEO content across multiple channels.

cards.title: Monitor AI Search Visibility with an LLM Brand Monitor
cards.summary: Track whether your brand appears in AI overviews and LLM responses, and how it is sentiment-ranked across those platforms.
cards.use_when: Measuring AI search (AEO) presence and brand visibility beyond traditional rank tracking.

cards.title: Choose Category Content Structure for AI Overviews
cards.summary: Structure article formatting so content is more likely to be pulled into AI overviews and LLM answers.
cards.use_when: Configuring article templates and on-page formatting for SEO content meant to surface in AI-driven search results.

cards.title: Auto-Generate Branded Infographics for Content
cards.summary: Prompt the AI workflow to create on-brand infographics and schedule them alongside social posts.
cards.use_when: Producing visual content for social distribution without a dedicated designer.

cards.title: Keep Human Approval Gates in Automated Content Pipelines
cards.summary: Insert approval steps between concept generation, article creation, and publishing to catch errors while preserving automation speed.
cards.use_when: Building or running an end-to-end AI content pipeline and deciding where a human should review.

cards.title: Layer Multiple AI Tools Rather Than Relying on One
cards.summary: Combine a general AI agent with a specialized SEO writer and a scheduler so each tool does what it does best.
cards.use_when: Designing an AI content stack and deciding whether one tool is enough.

cards.title: Answer-engine shift: optimize to be cited, not just clicked
cards.summary: Reframe SEO goals from ranking one blue link to being the trusted source cited by AI answer engines, while keeping traditional rankings as the entry ticket.
cards.use_when: Deciding overall SEO/content strategy and how to measure success for a store's organic channel as AI Overviews, GPT search and Perplexity reduce click-through to product and category pages.

cards.title: Keep keyword research simple: two buckets only
cards.summary: Find only transactional (buying-intent) and informational (topical-authority) keywords and stop overcomplicating.
cards.use_when: Starting keyword research for a store's category and product pages or planning a blog/content engine.

cards.title: Mine low-difficulty, high-volume 'gold nugget' keywords
cards.summary: Scan keyword lists for terms with low/near-zero keyword difficulty and high search volume, then build a dedicated page plus supporting content.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing which new product/category or landing pages to build first when you have limited resources and a new or low-authority site.

cards.title: Generate unlimited content ideas with question-mining tools
cards.summary: Use question-clustering tools to turn one topic into hundreds of FAQ-driven blog posts, each mapped to a real search question.
cards.use_when: Filling out a store's content calendar with buyer-education articles that capture research-stage shoppers and build topical authority.

cards.title: Run lean competitor keyword and backlink analysis in one spreadsheet
cards.summary: Compare 3–4 competitors' estimated traffic, backlink counts and ranked keywords in a single view to surface keyword gaps you can win.
cards.use_when: Finding product/category or location pages rivals rank for that you don't, before deciding what to build next.

cards.title: Use AI to turn messy keyword data into an actionable page plan
cards.summary: Prompt an LLM with raw keyword exports and business context to output a structured map of main pages, subpages and articles.
cards.use_when: Translating a spreadsheet full of keywords into concrete page targets for a product/category/service site before you start building.

cards.title: Plan website architecture before building ('measure twice, cut once')
cards.summary: Design the full page hierarchy, URLs, titles and internal links in a spreadsheet/sitemap before touching any site builder.
cards.use_when: Launching or restructuring an online store's information architecture so categories, subcategories and products map to search intent cleanly.

cards.title: Build hub, subservice and location pages that match search intent
cards.summary: Structure main-service/location pages with consistent on-page sections while varying subservice and location to capture transactional demand.
cards.use_when: Creating category or 'service in [location]' landing pages (adaptable to store categories by location or product type) that need to rank for high-intent terms.

cards.title: High-quality AI content workflow: negative keyword list, tone-of-voice doc, preliminary-question prompt
cards.summary: A repeatable AI-assisted writing workflow that keeps output on-brand and well-sourced instead of generic AI fluff.
cards.use_when: You need to produce blog or category copy for your store at volume without it reading like generic AI content.

cards.title: Surviving AI search overviews: unique voice, sourced data, simple language, visuals
cards.summary: GEO principles for getting cited in AI overviews, GPT search and Perplexity, summarised from a Princeton GEO paper cited in the source.
cards.use_when: You are writing store content (category pages, buying guides, blog posts) that needs to be picked up by AI search results, not just classic SERPs.

cards.title: Add supporting visuals to content with Napkin.ai and ship them as WebP
cards.summary: Turn a text section into a simple explanatory visual and upload it in an optimised image format.
cards.use_when: A product or blog section is hard to grasp from text alone and would benefit from a diagram before you publish the page.

cards.title: Two types of links every content page needs: external citation + internal money page
cards.summary: Content that ranks and converts must cite external sources for its claims and internally link to the commercial page it supports.
cards.use_when: You're publishing a blog or guide for your store and want it to drive traffic to category or service pages.

cards.title: Pillar-and-satellite content plan for an ecommerce or service store
cards.summary: Structure a topic cluster around one main page plus supporting articles that all link back to it.
cards.use_when: You're planning the content calendar or site architecture for a store and want topical authority around a core product or destination.

cards.title: Scale content production with a cluster tool (Machined AI workflow)
cards.summary: Use a clustering tool to generate a batch of interrelated posts in your tone of voice, then edit them rather than publishing raw output.
cards.use_when: You need many supporting articles produced quickly for a category, destination or service cluster.

cards.title: Don't buy 'our content ranks number one' promises — learn the fundamentals instead
cards.summary: Tool choice matters less than understanding what makes content good; distrust tools advertising guaranteed rankings.
cards.use_when: You're evaluating an AI content tool or agency for your store's content production.

cards.title: Local SEO fundamentals: Google Business Profile, citations, locality on site
cards.summary: Three non-negotiable pillars that drive local visibility for a store with a physical presence or service area.
cards.use_when: You run a local store or service-area business and need a prioritised local SEO plan.

cards.title: Optimise the Google Business Profile: categories, images to 100, weekly posts, reviews
cards.summary: Operate the GBP like an active social account, with category accuracy, image volume, posts and easy review capture.
cards.use_when: You've claimed your store's GBP and want it to actually drive calls, direction requests and site visits.

cards.title: Running a local citation campaign with NAP consistency
cards.summary: Find, submit and track local directory listings so the same name, address and phone appear everywhere.
cards.use_when: You're building local trust for a new store or a store that has changed name, address or phone number.

cards.title: Localise on-site content: put the location into titles, H1s and metadata
cards.summary: A .com.au domain alone isn't granular enough — every service page and heading should name the city.
cards.use_when: You're optimising service or category pages for a specific city or region.

cards.title: Technical SEO scope plus speed checks with two tools
cards.summary: What falls under technical SEO, and how to measure page speed without a biased result.
cards.use_when: You're auditing your store's site and need to decide what to check first and what to escalate to a developer.

cards.title: Prioritize site speed fixes before other SEO work
cards.summary: Diagnose page load speed with GTmetrix and PageSpeed Insights, then fix the slowest culprits first because speed drives both rankings and purchase conversions.
cards.use_when: Auditing an online store's technical SEO and deciding what to fix first, especially before investing in content or links.

cards.title: Convert and compress product images to WebP
cards.summary: Shrink heavy product images by converting PNG/JPG to WebP or compressing them, which speeds up pages and reduces bounce, without visible quality loss.
cards.use_when: Speeding up a store's category or product pages where oversized images are the identified bottleneck in a speed report.

cards.title: Audit title tags, meta descriptions and H1s with a browser extension
cards.summary: Use a free on-page SEO extension (e.g., SEO Wallet) to check each money page's title, meta description, H1 and heading order against clear rules.
cards.use_when: Reviewing on-page SEO across a store's homepage, category pages and top product pages before content or link work.

cards.title: Add schema markup to money pages to clarify page content
cards.summary: Inject JSON-LD structured data (Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, etc.) into key pages so search engines instantly know a page's subject, aiding rankings and rich results.
cards.use_when: Improving how search engines understand a store's homepage, category pages and product pages, especially before or alongside content work.

cards.title: Make the first fold instantly communicate offer and next action
cards.summary: Cut above-the-fold ambiguity so visitors immediately grasp what the store sells and the one action to take, because scrolling loses a large share of visitors.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a store homepage, category or landing page hero to raise purchase or lead conversion from existing traffic.

cards.title: Win backlinks via journalist-source matching (Featured) as free outreach
cards.summary: Earn high-quality editorial backlinks by answering journalist questions on platforms like Featured (formerly HARO), prioritizing relevance and real experience.
cards.use_when: Building free, relevant backlinks to a store's category or content pages when budget is limited but time is available.

cards.title: Judge backlink quality: relevance over quantity and natural link growth
cards.summary: Prefer one relevant link from a reputable site over many spammy ones, and screen prospects for unnatural referring-domain spikes.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to buy, accept or build a backlink, and vetting any link-building vendor or prospect.

cards.title: Buy backlinks from vetted vendors when competitors outrank you
cards.summary: If a competitive niche demands links and organic outreach is too slow, purchase links from reputable vendors with relevant industry packages and track them by anchor, target URL and source.
cards.use_when: Considering paid link building for a store in a competitive niche where competitors clearly dominate backlinks.

cards.title: Separate Search Console (how Google sees you) from Analytics (what visitors do)
cards.summary: Use Search Console for rankings, queries and indexing, and Analytics for traffic sources and on-site behavior — pulling the two apart stops metric confusion.
cards.use_when: Setting up or interpreting search and site performance data for an online store to decide next actions.

cards.title: Mine positions 9–30 in Search Console for low-hanging SEO wins
cards.summary: Find pages already ranking on page 2+ and improve them with updated content, internal links or targeted backlinks, which is faster than ranking new pages.
cards.use_when: Planning the next month's SEO work on a store's existing pages when you are unsure where to start.

cards.title: Use Analytics traffic-source data to find partner and acquisition opportunities
cards.summary: Examine which referral and channel sources send quality converting traffic, then deepen or replicate those sources rather than chasing raw volume.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest acquisition or partnership effort for an online store by reviewing real source performance.

cards.title: Ignore domain authority as a vanity metric; judge by keywords and conversions
cards.summary: Domain authority/ranking is a third-party composite that does not map to the bottom line, so track rankings for target keywords and actual conversions instead.
cards.use_when: Choosing which SEO KPIs to report or optimize when evaluating a store's website performance.

cards.title: Turn raw SEO data into actions with an AI analyst
cards.summary: Export Search Console/Analytics data and feed it to an AI analyst to get prioritized, actionable recommendations and seasonal patterns instead of drowning in spreadsheets.
cards.use_when: Monthly SEO review for an online store when you have the data but are unsure what to do with it.
